text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah plans a cabinet-parliament meeting to improve cooperation between lawmakers and the government. MPs have bitterly criticised the government's performance in fighting alleged corruption following an attempt on the life of an opposition MP earlier in June.

- Planning Minister Ali al-Zmei'a asks government bodies to launch a previously-announced plan to gradually replace foreign state workers with Kuwaitis. The plan, which would be launched as of June 30, aims to give 10 percent of state jobs held by expatriates to nationals each year.
- The Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah to discuss on Tuesday bilateral cooperation with visiting Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov.
- Kuwait's Court of Cassation upholds death sentence against two Egyptians convicted of murdering a Kuwaiti man. Death sentence requires the approval of the emir before they can be executed.
- Kuwait's real estate market witnesses increased demand. Only nationals of the six Gulf Arab states can trade in Kuwaiti property.
- Iranian official sources say Kuwait's Emir to take part in Islamic summit to be held in Tehran later on December 1997.

- Three MPs recommend that the government should suspend plans to shed stakes at Kuwaiti firms until parliament issues a law setting privatisation rules. The state, which sold stakes worth about $2.4 billion since the 1994 launch of its wide-ranging privatisation programme, plans to sell shares worth about three billion dollars.

- New mobile telecomunications firm to be launched with a 30-million-dinar ($100 million) capital. Currently Mobile Telecommunications Co (MTC) is the sole provider of mobile telephones and pagers service in the tiny Gulf state.
